sections.english: The substance of the Whole is passive and malleable, and the reason directing this substance has no cause in itself to do wrong, as there is no wrong in it: nothing it creates is wrongly made, nothing harmed by it. All things have their beginning and their end in accordance with it.
sections.chinese: 宇宙整体之实体是顺从并可塑的，而引导此实体之理性本身并无作恶之由，因其内毫无邪恶：它所创生之物无一被造错，无一受其损害。万物皆依照它而有其起始与终结。

sections.english: If you are doing your proper duty let it not matter to you whether you are cold or warm, whether you are sleepy or well-slept, whether men speak badly or well of you, even whether you are on the point of death or doing something else: because even this, the act of dying, is one of the acts of life. So it is enough 'to make the best of this move on to the next'.
sections.chinese: 若你正在执行你之本分，便无谓你或冷或暖，无论困倦抑或已得饱睡，无论人言于你是好是恶，甚至无论你是临死之际或正做他事：因为即便是死亡这一行为，亦乃生命之诸行为之一。故「善用当前之一步，随即转入下一步」，便已足够。

sections.english: Look within: do not allow the special quality or worth of any thing to pass you by.
sections.chinese: 反观于内：莫令任何事物之独特品性或价值从你眼下滑过。

sections.english: All that exists will soon change. Either it will be turned into vapour, if all matter is a unity, or it will be scattered in atoms.
sections.chinese: 一切现存者皆将迅速改变。若所有物质是一整体，则化为蒸气；否则便散为原子。

sections.english: The governing reason knows its own disposition, what it creates, and what is the material for its creation.
sections.chinese: 那统御之理性知晓自身之性向，知晓它创生何物，亦知晓其创造所用之材料为何。

sections.english: The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.
sections.chinese: 最佳之复仇，便是不像你的仇敌那般。

sections.english: Let one thing be your joy and comfort: to move on from social act to social act, with your mind on god.
sections.chinese: 让一件事成为你的快乐与慰藉：自一社会性行动转向另一社会性行动，心思常念神明。

sections.english: The directing mind is that which wakes itself, adapts itself, makes itself of whatever nature it wishes, and makes all that happens to it appear in the way it wants.
sections.chinese: 主导心灵乃是自我唤醒者、自我调适者——它令自己成为所愿之任何性质，并使发生在其上之一切皆依其所愿之方式显现。

sections.english: All things have their accomplishment in accordance with the nature of the Whole: it could not be in accordance with any other nature, either enclosing from without or enclosed within, or any external influence.
sections.chinese: 万物皆依照宇宙整体之本性而成就：这不可能是依照任何其他本然——无论是自外包裹的，或内嵌其中的，抑或任何外在影响。

sections.english: Either a stew, an intricate web, and dispersal into atoms: or unity, order, and providence. Now if the former, why do I even wish to spend my time in a world compounded at random and in like confusion? Why have any concern other than somehow, some time, to 'return to earth'? And why am I troubled? Dispersal will come to me, whatever I do. But if the latter, I am reverent, I am resolute, I put my trust in the governor.
sections.chinese: 要么是一锅乱炖、一张纷繁之网，以及离散为原子；要么是统一、秩序，与天意。若是前者，我何苦要活在一个偶然混成、秩序同样混乱的世界里？除了在某一刻、以某种方式「复归于尘土」之外，我还有何事可关切？我又为何烦恼？无论我怎样做，离散终究会临到我。然而，若是后者，我心怀虔敬，我坚定不移，我寄信任于那统御者。

sections.english: When circumstances force you to some sort of distress, quickly return to yourself. Do not stay out of rhythm for longer than you must: you will master the harmony the more by constantly going back to it.
sections.chinese: 当际遇迫使你陷入某种忧苦，迅速回到你自己。勿在律动之外停留过你所必需要之久：恒常回归和律之中，你便会越发掌握其和谐。

sections.english: If you had a step-mother and a mother at the same time, you would pay attention to your step-mother but nevertheless your constant recourse would be to your mother. That is now how it is with the Court and philosophy. So return to philosophy again and again, and find your rest in her: through her the life of the Court seems bearable to you, and you seem bearable in it.
sections.chinese: 若你同时有继母与生母，你会对继母有所顾应，但你不断返归的仍会是你的生母。宫廷与哲学，现在即是如此。故当时时复归于哲学，在她之中获你之安息：藉由她，宫廷之生活对你才显得可堪忍受，而你在此生活之中，亦显得可堪忍受。

sections.english: How good it is, when you have roast meat or suchlike foods before you, to impress on your mind that this is the dead body of a fish, this the dead body of a bird or pig; and again, that the Falernian wine is the mere juice of grapes, and your purple-edged robe simply sheep's wool dipped in shellfish blood; and in sexual intercourse that it is no more than the friction of a membrane and a spurt of mucus ejected. How good these perceptions are at penetrating to the heart of the thing and laying it bare!
sections.chinese: 当你面前摆着烤肉之类食物时，能于心中印下此念——此为鱼之尸身，此乃禽鸟或猪之尸身；再者，法勒恩葡萄酒不过是葡萄之汁液，你那镶紫边的长袍不过是羊皮浸于贝血之中；至于交合之事，不过一层薄膜之摩擦与一股黏液之迸射——如此观之，何其善也！这些观照能穿透事物之核心，令其赤裸暴露，何其善也！

sections.english: Most of the things valued by the masses come under the categories of what is sustained by cohesion (minerals, timber) or natural growth (figs, vines, olives). What is valued by the slightly more advanced belongs to the class of things sustained by a conscious life — flocks, herds, slaves. What is valued by the yet more sophisticated is governed by a rational life — not the Reason of the Whole, but the technical or otherwise skilled reason. But the man who honours the soul in full possession of all these other qualities, the soul that is rational and fit for society and the community, has no concern for anything else: above all he keeps his own soul in the full and constant persuasion of reason and social action, and works with his fellow man to the same end.
sections.chinese: 大众所珍视之物，大多归于靠凝聚而维系之类别（矿石、木材）或自然生长之类别（无花果、藤蔓、橄榄）。稍为进步者所珍视的，则属于靠有意识生命而维系者——羊群、牛群、奴隶。更为精熟者所珍视的，由一种理性生命所统御——非宇宙整体之理性，而是技术或某种其他娴熟技能之理性。然而，那尊崇完满地拥有其他一切品质之灵魂——即那种合乎理性且宜于社会与共同体的灵魂——的人，对任何别物皆漠不关心：首要者，他保持己之灵魂全然且恒常立于理性与社会行动之信念中，并与同侪携手共赴同一目的。

sections.english: Some things are hurrying to come into being, others are hurrying to be gone, and part of that which is being born is already extinguished. Flows and changes are constantly renewing the world, just as the ceaseless passage of time makes eternity ever young. In this river, then, where there can be no foothold, what should any of these things hurtling past mean to us? No more than if we fell in love with a sparrow flitting by: already it has vanished from sight.
sections.chinese: 有物急急生成，有物急急消逝，而新生者之一部分已然熄灭。流转与变化不断更新世界，正如时间之不止流逝令永恒永葆青春。那么，在此无立足之处的河流中，这些飞掠而过之物对我们又有何意义？不比我们爱上一只倏然飞过之麻雀更真切：转瞬之间，它已消失于眼帘。

sections.english: Up, down, round and round are the motions of the elements, but the movement of active virtue follows none of these: it is something more divine, and it journeys on to success along a path hard to understand.
sections.chinese: 元素之运动，或上升、或下降、或回环旋转，然而活跃之美德其运动却不循此轨：它乃是更近于神性之物，沿一条难于领悟之路，前行以至成就。

sections.english: What a way to behave! They refuse to speak well of people who live as their contemporaries and in their company, but they set great store by their own good name among future generations which they have never seen nor ever will see. Yet this is brother to grieving that our praises were not sung by past generations.
sections.chinese: 何等之做派！他们不肯说与己同时同处之人的好话，却恋恋于自己在后代人中——后者他们从未见过，也永不会见——之名声。然而，这与为昔日之人未曾歌咏我们而悲伤，又有何异。

sections.english: Do not imagine that, if something is hard for you to achieve, it is therefore impossible for any man: but rather consider anything that is humanly possible and appropriate to lie within your own reach too.
sections.chinese: 不要以为，若某事对你来说难于达成，它便对任何人而言皆是不可行的：反之，你应当设想：凡在人而言为可能且恰当之事，亦在你自身所能及之范围内。

sections.english: In the field of play an opponent scratches us with his nails, say, or gives us a butting blow with his head: but we do not 'mark' him for that, or take offence, or suspect him afterwards of deliberate attack. True, we do keep clear of him: but this is not as an enemy or with suspicion — we give him a wide berth in a peaceful way. Let this be the way we view things in the other areas of life: let us overlook much of the behaviour of our opponents in the game. As I said, we can keep clear, but without suspicion or hatred.
sections.chinese: 赛场上，对手或许以指甲抓伤我们，或以头撞击我们，但我们不因此便盯记他，不动怒，也不事后疑他蓄意攻击。固然，我们确实会避开他：但这并非如待仇敌那般或心存猜疑——我们是以平和之方式保持距离。以此方式来看待我们生活其他领域之事吧：对那些在比赛中与我们对抗者之种种举动，多数都可略过。如我所说，我们可保持距避，但无猜疑、无恨憎。

sections.english: If someone can prove me wrong and show me my mistake in any thought or action, I shall gladly change. I seek the truth, which never harmed anyone: the harm is to persist in one's own self-deception and ignorance.
sections.chinese: 若有人能证明我错了，指出我在某种思想或行动中之过错，我必欣然改变。我寻求真理，真理从未伤害任何人：伤害在于固执于己之自欺与无知。

sections.english: I do my own duty: the other things do not distract me. They are either inanimate or irrational, or have lost the road and are ignorant of the true way.
sections.chinese: 我尽我之本分：其他事物不能令我动摇。它们或无生、或无理性，或者已迷失路途，不知真正之道。

sections.english: Since you have reason and they do not, treat dumb animals and generally all things and objects with generosity and decency; treat men, because they do have reason, with social concern; and in all things call on the gods.
sections.chinese: 你拥有理性而它们没有，故当以宽厚与端正之心对待哑畜、及一般之物与用器；对待人——因他们有理性——则以社会性之关切；并在一切事上呼请诸神。

sections.english: Alexander of Macedon and his muleteer were levelled in death: either they were taken up into the same generative principles of the universe, or they were equally dispersed into atoms.
sections.chinese: 马其顿的亚历山大与其骡夫，在死亡中归于齐平：他们要么被纳入宇宙同一之创生原理，要么同样散为原子。

sections.english: Reflect on how many separate events, both bodily and mental, are taking place in each one of us in the same tiny fragment of time: and then you will not be surprised if many more events, indeed all that comes to pass, subsist together in the one and entire Whole which we call the universe.
sections.chinese: 试思在每一人身上，在同一微末时间里，发生着多少彼此分离之事件——无论身体上与心灵上：如此，你便不会惊异，若有远为更多之事件——事实上，所有发生之事——一并存在于那我们称为宇宙之独一而完整之整体中。

sections.english: If someone puts to you the question 'How is the name Antoninus spelt?', will you shout your way through each of the syllables? What then if they get angry? Will you lose your temper too? Will you not rather calmly go through the sequence of letters, enumerating each one? So in life too, remember that every duty is made up of its constituent parts. These you must observe; without discomposure or mutual indignation you must complete in methodical order your appointed task.
sections.chinese: 若有人问你：「安东尼努斯之名如何拼写？」，你会逐个字母咆哮喊出吗？倘若他们发怒了呢？你也会大发脾气吗？你难道不会冷静地逐一列出字母顺序吗？在生活中也是如此，记住每一职责皆由其诸构成部分所组成。你须关注这些部分；不受扰乱，不激发彼此怒气，你必须按部就班地完成指派于你的任务。

sections.english: How cruel it is not to allow people to strive for what seems to them their interest and advantage! And yet in a way you are forbidding them to do this, when you fuss that they are wrong: they are surely drawn to their own interest and advantage. 'But it is not so.' Then demonstrate that and teach them, without being put out.
sections.chinese: 不许人去追求那些在他们看来是己之利益与好处的事，何其残忍！然而在某方面，当你对他们的错误耿耿于怀时，你便正是禁止他们这样做：他们确是被自己的利益与好处所吸引。「可情况并非如此。」那么，便证明这一点并教导他们吧，而无需动气。

sections.english: Death is relief from reaction to the senses, from the puppet-strings of impulse, from the analytical mind, and from service to the flesh.
sections.chinese: 死亡乃是从感官之反应、冲动之提线木偶、分析之心灵，以及对肉身之役事中的解脱。

sections.english: Disgraceful if, in this life where your body does not fail, your soul should fail you first. Take care not to be Caesarified, or dyed in purple: it happens. So keep yourself simple, good, pure, serious, unpretentious, a friend of justice, god-fearing, kindly, affectionate, strong for your proper work.
sections.chinese: 若在此一生中，你的躯体尚未不济，而你的灵魂却先你而衰败，那真是可耻。留神切勿被凯撒化，或被染成紫色：这样的事情确实发生。故当保持自己素朴、善良、纯净、严肃、不务虚饰、做正义之友、敬神、仁慈、深情、且坚毅于你之本分工作。

sections.english: Sober up, recall yourself, shake off sleep once more: realize they were mere dreams that troubled you, and now that you are awake again look on these things as you would have looked on a dream.
sections.chinese: 清醒过来，召回你自己，再一次抖落沉眠：明白那些搅扰你的不过是些梦境，而既然你已然再次醒着，便以你在梦中看待它们之方式来看待这些事。

sections.english: I am made of body and soul. Now to the poor body all things are indifferent, as it cannot even make any distinction. To the mind all that is not its own activity is indifferent: and its own activities are all in its control. But within these the mind only concerns itself with the present: its future or past activities are themselves indifferent now.
sections.chinese: 我由身体与灵魂所构成。对于这可怜的身体，一切皆漠不相干，因它甚至不能作任何区分。对于心灵，凡非其自身活动者，皆漠不相干：而其自身活动，皆在其掌控之中。然而，即便在这些活动之中，心灵也仅专注于当下：它将来或过去的活动，在此刻自身也是漠不相干的。

sections.english: The pain of labour for hand or foot is not contrary to nature, as long as the foot is doing the work of a foot and the hand the work of a hand. So likewise for a man, qua man, there is nothing contrary to nature in pain, as long as he is doing the work of a man. And if not contrary to nature, then not an evil either.
sections.chinese: 手、足劳作之苦并不违背自然，只要足在做足之工，手在行手之活。于人而言亦是如此，只要他作为一个人在做人之事，痛苦之中便没有任何违背自然之处。若不违背自然，那也就不是恶。

sections.english: As for pleasure, pirates, catamites, parricides, and tyrants have enjoyed it to the full.
sections.chinese: 至于逸乐，海盗、娈童、弑亲者，以及暴君，皆曾享之至极。

sections.english: Do you not see how the working craftsman, while deferring to the layman up to a point, nevertheless sticks to the principle of his craft and will not bear to desert it? Is it not strange, then, that the architect and the doctor will show greater respect for the principle of their own crafts than man shows for his own reason, which he shares with the gods?
sections.chinese: 难道你没看见工匠在某种程度上虽对外行有所让步，却仍坚持其技艺之原则而不忍弃之？那么，建筑师和医生对各自技艺之原则所展现的尊重，比人对己身与诸神所共享之理性的尊重更甚，难道不奇怪吗？

sections.english: He who sees the present has seen all things, both all that has come to pass from everlasting and all that will be for eternity: all things are related and the same.
sections.chinese: 见当下者，即已见一切——既见了自永恒以来所发生之一切，也见了将在永恒中发生之一切：万物皆相连相通且同质。

sections.english: You should meditate often on the connection of all things in the universe and their relationship to each other. In a way all things are interwoven and therefore have a family feeling for each other: one thing follows another in due order through the tension of movement, the common spirit, and the unity of all substance.
sections.chinese: 当时时沉思宇宙万物之联系及其彼此之关系。在某种程度上，万物皆彼此交织，因而彼此间有一种亲属般之相亲感：一物依适当之秩序，通过运动之张力、共同之精神，以及一切实体之统一而顺次追随另一物。

sections.english: Fit yourself for the matters which have fallen to your lot, and love these people among whom destiny has cast you — but your love must be genuine.
sections.chinese: 令自己适配于命运所分派于你之事务，并爱命运将你投入其中之人们——但你的爱必须是真诚的。

sections.english: An instrument, a tool, a utensil — all these are fine if they perform the function for which they were made. And yet in such cases the maker is external to the object made. In the case of things held together by organic nature, the power that made them is within, and remains with them. So you should hold these in the greater reverence, reckoning that if you conduct and order your life by this power, then all within you is in accord with intelligence.
sections.chinese: 一件器械、一柄工具、一个器皿——若它们履行了其被造之功能，便都是好的。然而在此等情形中，制造者外在于被造之物。而在由有机自然所维系凝聚之事物中，那创生之力量乃在其内部，且与之同在。故你当以此更大之敬意来珍视它们，思量你若依此力量来引导并规整你之生命，则你内中一切皆与智性相符。

sections.english: If you set up as good or evil any of the things beyond your control, it necessarily follows that in the occurrence of that evil or the frustration of that good you blame the gods and hate the men who are the real or suspected causes of that occurrence or frustration. And indeed our frequent injustice to each other is caused by our making a distinction between these things. But if we judge only what is in our power to be good or evil, then there is no further reason either to blame god or to take a hostile stance to men.
sections.chinese: 若你将你掌控之外的任何事物定为好或坏，则必然的后果便是：当那坏事发生、或那好事受挫之时，你便谴责诸神，并仇恨那些造成此事发生或使其受挫的真实或可疑的人。而事实上，吾辈彼此间层出不穷之非义，正是由于我们在此等事物之间妄作区分。若我们仅判断那在我们权能之内者为好或坏，则既无由再责神，亦无由敌对他人。

sections.english: We all work together to the same end, some with conscious attention, others without knowing it — just as Heraclitus, I think, says that even people asleep are workers in the factory of all that happens in the world.
sections.chinese: 吾辈皆协同工作，朝向同一目标——有些人有觉知地关注，有些人则在不知中为之——正如赫拉克利特所言，我想，即便是沉睡之人，也乃是世间所发生一切之工厂中的工人。

sections.english: Does the sun presume to do the work of the rain-god, or Asclepius that of the goddess of harvest? And what of each of the stars? Is it not that they are different, but work together to the same end?
sections.chinese: 太阳岂敢去做雨神之工作？阿斯克勒庇俄斯又去做丰收女神之事？而每颗星辰又复如何？它们岂不是彼此不同，然却协同工作朝向同一目的？

sections.english: All that happens to the individual is to the benefit of the Whole. So far, so clear. But if you look more closely you will also see as a general rule that what benefits one person benefits other people too — though here 'benefit' should be taken in its common application to things indifferent.
sections.chinese: 凡临到个体之事，皆有益于总体。到此为止，尚算清楚。但若你更细细去看，你还会见出一条通则：那有益于一人者，亦有益于他人——虽说此处「有益」一词当依其通常应用于漠不相干之物之意义来解。

sections.english: Just as all the business of the amphitheatre and such places offends you as always one and the same sight, and this monotony of the spectacle bores you, so it is too with your experience of life as a whole: everything, up or down, is the same, with the same causes. For how long, then?
sections.chinese: 正如斗兽场及类似场所之诸般事务令你生厌——总是一再相同之景象，此等景象之单调令你厌倦——你之整个生命经验亦复如此：一切，无论上下高低，皆相同，皆有相同之因由。那么，又能多久呢？

sections.english: Whenever you want to cheer yourself, think of the qualities of your fellows — the energy of one, for example, the decency of another, the generosity of a third, some other merit in a fourth. There is nothing so cheering as the stamp of virtues manifest in the characters of those around us. So we should keep these ready to hand.
sections.chinese: 每当你想要鼓舞自己时，想想你同侪之质量——譬如，一人的精力、另一人的端正、第三人的慷慨、第四人的某种其他长处。世间无物比我们周围人品性中所显现之美德印记更能鼓舞人。故我们当将这些随时备在左右。

sections.english: You do not resent your weight, do you — that you weigh only so many pounds and not three hundred? So why resent either a life-span of so many years and not more? Just as you are content with the amount of matter allocated to you, so you should be content with your allocation of time.
sections.chinese: 你并不怨恨你的体重，对吧——你只有这么些磅而非三百磅？那么，又何必怨恨寿命仅有这么些年而非更长久呢？正如你满足于分配到你的物质量，你也当满足于分配给你的时间量。

sections.english: Try to persuade them, but act even if they are unpersuaded, whenever the principle of justice so directs. But if someone forcibly resists, change tack to an unhurt acceptance, so using the obstacle to bring forth a different virtue. And remember that your impulse was conditional — you were not aiming at the impossible. At what then? Just at making the attempt itself. So you have achieved your object: what our own impulse aimed at is achieved.
sections.chinese: 尽力去说服他们，但若正义原则如此指引，即便他们未被说服，也当行动。若有人强力抗拒，便转换态度，转为一种不致受创之接纳，以利用障碍引出另一种美德。并记住：你的冲动原是有条件的——你并非志在不可企及之事。那你志在什么？不过志在此番尝试本身。如此，你已实现了你的目标：我们自己冲动之指向已得实现。

sections.english: How to understand your own good: the lover of glory takes it to be the reactions of others; the lover of pleasure takes it to be his own passive experience; the intelligent man sees it as his own action.
sections.chinese: 如何理解自己之善好：爱荣耀者以他人之反应为善好；爱逸乐者以己之被动经验为善好；而有智之士则以自己之行动为善好。

sections.english: It is possible to have no understanding of this and not to be troubled in mind: things of themselves have no inherent power to form our judgements.
sections.chinese: 不解此理亦可不致心烦意乱：事物本身并没有形成我们判断之固有力量。

sections.english: Accustom yourself not to be disregarding of what someone else has to say: as far as possible enter into the mind of the speaker.
sections.chinese: 养成习惯：勿轻忽他人所言之语；尽可能深入言说者之心。

sections.english: What does not benefit the hive does not benefit the bee either.
sections.chinese: 于蜂巢无益者，于蜂亦无益。

sections.english: If sailors spoke ill of their captain or patients of their doctor, who else would they listen to? Otherwise how would the captain achieve a safe voyage for his passengers or the doctor health for those in his care?
sections.chinese: 若水手说其船长之歹话，或病患说其医生之歹话，他们还能听从谁呢？若非如此，船长何以令乘客安全航行，医生何以令人康复于其看护之中？

sections.english: How many with whom I came into the world have already left!
sections.chinese: 多少与我一同来到此世之人，已然离去！

sections.english: Appearances: to the jaundiced honey seems bitter, to those bitten by rabid dogs water is a terror, to little boys a ball is joy. Why then am I angry? Or do you think that false representation has less effect than bile in the jaundiced or poison in the rabid?
sections.chinese: 表象之效力：于患黄疸者，蜜似为苦；于被疯狗咬伤者，水可恐可怖；于小男孩，一颗球便是欢欣。那么，我为何动怒？莫非你以为虚假之呈现，其效力比黄疸病人之胆汁或狂犬病人之毒来得更弱？

sections.english: No one will prevent you living in accordance with the principle of your own nature: nothing will happen to you contrary to the principle of universal nature.
sections.chinese: 无人能阻挡你依照你自身本性之原则而生活；没有事情会违背宇宙本性之原则而临到你身。

sections.english: What sort of people they wish to please! And what kind of actions are the means of their success! How quickly time will cover everything — and how much is covered already.
sections.chinese: 他们想要取悦的是何等样人！而他们用以成功之手段又是何等样之行动！时间将何其迅速地淹没一切——又有多少早已被淹没。
